Featured Managers

Manager snapshot
Dave F.
Dave F. is the standard setter for the whole league: 6 titles, 17 playoff trips, and enough elite seasons to anchor the entire history view.
Manager snapshot
Brian B
Brian B was a repeat finisher, not a one-shot champion. 4 titles and 10 podiums make this one of the era-defining resumes.
Manager snapshot
Chris P.
Chris P. was a repeat finisher, not a one-shot champion. 2 titles and 7 podiums make this one of the era-defining resumes.

Elissa P.

Manager snapshot
Jason P.

Head-to-Head

Not every frequent matchup is a rivalry. This section tries to isolate the ones that actually mattered: close series, repeat playoff collisions, and pairings where one manager became the other’s recurring problem.

Defining rivalry
Brian B vs Dave F.
42 games across 23 seasons, with 8 playoff meetings. Brian B has usually had the edge, but the real story is that this matchup kept mattering for a long time.
Closest long-run matchup
Andrew P. vs Jason P.
24 meetings across 15 seasons with an average margin of 16.7 points. This is the tightest rivalry that also held up over time.
Playoff foil
Brian B vs Dave F.
8 playoff meetings across 42 total games. This is the rivalry to read if you care about blocked title paths more than regular-season volume.
How To Read Rivalries
  • Start with the defining rivalry to see which matchup held weight across the most seasons, not just the smallest average margin.
  • Use closest long-run matchup when you want the tightest rivalry that also lasted.
  • Tightest long-running matchups require at least 10 games across 8 seasons and a reasonably balanced series record; average margin is the mean absolute score difference per meeting.
  • Use playoff foils when you care about who blocked title paths, not just who played often.
  • Use the heat map as a scan tool, then open the full matrix when you want the exact record and margin.

Data Quality

This section is here to protect trust. Older seasons still matter, but when the history is partial or suspect, the report should say so plainly instead of quietly letting shaky rows rewrite the story.

Minimum multi-season sample
3
Used for trends, classifications, and legacy comps
Suspect matchups
40
Flagged for zero/missing scores, hidden managers, or invalid results
Suspect seasons
1
Excluded from record-book lows when totals are clearly incomplete
Integrity checks
1 failing
Sanity checks like championships, podiums, and playoff trips never exceeding seasons
Partial player-data years
2003
Excluded from player record-book sections when player scoring cannot be trusted
  • Headline records are filtered to remove clearly suspect rows such as zero-point team games and hidden-manager rows.
  • Historical anomalies are retained in validation tables so we can clean them over time instead of pretending the data is clean.
  • Cross-era comparisons require a multi-season sample before a manager appears in consistency and classification views.
  • Player-level record sections exclude partial player-data seasons such as 2003.
